lead: The rolling year is characterized by active EFB and flight planning platform adoption across major and regional carriers, alongside significant corporate development maneuvers such as Lufthansa Systems exploring the sale of its Lido and NetLine units.

insights.title: IFS Secures Multiple EFB Wins
insights.finding: IFS expanded its EFBOne footprint by signing agreements with low-cost carrier MY FREIGHTER (Centrum Air), fastjet, and TUS Airways.
insights.aviation_context: IFS targets both regional and low-cost operators for cockpit digitalization.

insights.title: Aviobook Signs Royal Air Maroc
insights.finding: Thales subsidiary Aviobook secured a five-year agreement to supply Royal Air Maroc with the AvioBook Flight EFB platform.
insights.aviation_context: Flag carriers continue to modernize cockpit operations through long-term EFB vendor contracts.

insights.title: Jeppesen Dispatch Expansion
insights.finding: Jeppesen secured major flight planning agreements with Korean Air and Corendon Airlines for its dispatch and EFFCore suites.
insights.aviation_context: Integration covers large mixed-fleet operations and automated planning workflows.
insights.caveat: Migration periods for multi-fleet rollouts can span multiple quarters.

insights.title: Lufthansa Systems Explores Lido Unit Sale
insights.finding: Lufthansa Systems initiated a potential divestment process for its Lido and NetLine business units, valued at approximately €1bn.
insights.aviation_context: Divestment of core flight operations software divisions could reshape competitive dynamics in flight planning and navigation.

insights.title: Navblue Integrates Skywise Suite
insights.finding: Navblue expanded its collaborative offerings with TransNusa under the integrated Skywise Core X2 and S.FP+ platform.
insights.aviation_context: Airbus-backed solutions combine technical and flight operations data streams.
insights.caveat: Adoption scope is limited to specific regional deployments.
